Cautiously positive on growth and employment, dovish on inflation—with added caution from the FSR. The FOMC noted solid job gains and moderate activity but inflation below 2% and soft business fixed investment, and held the funds rate at 2.25–2.50% while highlighting increased uncertainties; Bullard’s dissent for a 25 bp cut underscored downside risk management. The FSR context tempers the outlook further: economic fundamentals influencing market liquidity and valuations, reduced investor appetite for corporate bonds, and declining 10-year Treasury yields point to risk-sensitive financing conditions; leveraged-loan vulnerabilities tied to credit standards add to downside skew even as stress-test results suggest core bank resilience. Net: activity mildly positive, inflation and investment soft, and financial conditions consistent with patience/easing—slightly more cautious than the baseline.
